Someone Paid Toyota Corolla Money for This F80 BMW M3, Sports Sedan Was Over $70K New
17 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
If you are shopping for a relatively modern sports sedan and the F80 BMW M3 sits at the top of your list, then you just missed your change to buy this example, which recently changed hands in the States.
The vehicle was listed on Cars&Bids as part of an online auction that ended on November 24, 2026, and it fetched $27,262. That’s pretty much new-gen Toyota Corolla money, as mentioned in the title, with the 2027 model year compact sedan having an MSRP of $23,325 for the base trim level. As for the M3 in question, it is an older one, as it’s a 2015 model year, though it has never been involved in an accident.
It also does not have any mileage discrepancies, as the Carfax history report, yet it has seen plenty of action, as it had 104,500 miles (168,200 km) on the odometer at the time of cataloging. The BMW M3 in question has a clean Florida title. The known flaws include the chips and scratches on the outside, curb rash on the wheels, a sagging headliner, and wear on the seats and interior touch point, the listing reveals.
Photo: Cars&Bids This German sports sedan also features a few mods, with the notable ones including the new rod bearings and rod bolts. Power is supplied by a familiar straight-six twin-turbocharged engine. The 3.0-liter unit developed 425 hp (431 ps/317 kW) and 406 lb-ft (550 Nm) of torque when the car was new. The 0-60 mph (0-97 kph) took 3.9 seconds with the 7-speed DCT transmission, and 4.1 seconds with the stick shift, and this example features the latter.
Some of the equipment mentioned in the ad includes the 19-inch wheels (Style 437M), the Executive Package, heated front and rear seats with power adjustment for the driver and front passenger, carbon fiber trim, a rear sunshade, and a Harman Kardon sound system.
The BMW M3 in question had its engine oil and filter changed in April 2026, at 103,188 miles (166,065 km). That is also when the underbody panel deflector lips, the oil pan gasket, engine mounts, rod bolts, and rod bearings were replaced. In December 2025, the right front inner door handle was replaced, as well as the two rear tires, and an alignment was performed, at 100,613 miles (161,921 km). More service entries are being revealed in the ad an in the Carfax history report.
A 2015 BMW M3usually goes from $28,000 to $50,000 in today’s used car market Stateside, and this one went for pretty much nothing. The window sticker reveals that initially sold for $70,995. As for the seller, they reportedly bought it in October 2019. So, if you encountered this older M3 listed for $27,262, would you have bought it?
